text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Irish politician, CHARLES PARNELL, who led the Home Rule party in the British House of Commons, was born in 1846.
American blind, deaf and mute teacher, HELEN KELLER, was born in 1880.
The QUEEN MOTHER (LADY ELIZABETH ANGELA MARGUERITE BOWES-LYON), the wife of KING GEORGE VI of England, was born in 1900. In 1990 there were celebrations throughout London to mark her 90th birthday.

American songwriter DOC POMUS, who wrote many of the hits of the fifties and sixties, was born in 1925. His earliest successful songwriting effort with MORT SHUMAN, was "A Teenager in Love" for 'Dion and The Belmonts'. This was followed by hits for FABIAN, ANDY WILLIAMS, BOBBY DARIN, JIMMY CLANTON, 'The Drifters' and ELVIS PRESLEY.
'Beach Boy' BRUCE JOHNSTON was born in 1944. He joined the group in 1965 after performing in the 'Ripcords' and as half of 'BRUCE and TERRY' with TERRY MELCHER.
US bass player with 'B.T.Express' LOUIS RISBROOK was born in 1953.
** EVENTS **
1693 : The first women's magazine "Ladies Mercury"
was published.
1743 : In the War of the Austrian Succession, GEORGE
II of Britain defeated the French at Dettingen. He was the last British monarch to lead his troops into battle.
1787 : EDWARD GIBBON wrote the last lines of his
classic "Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire", which was published the following May.
1801 : In Egypt, British forces defeated the French
and took control of Cairo.
1844 : JOSEPH SMITH, American religious leader and
founder of the Mormon Church, was killed by a mob in an Illinois jail.
1905 : Mutinous Russian soldiers seized the
battleship Potemkin in the Black Sea, throwing the commander and several other officers overboard.
1939 : Pan-American airlines began its transatlantic
air service, with a 19-seater flying boat.
1949 : The national coal miners' strike began in
Australia.
1952 : A 32-year-old Sydney woman was charged with

murdering her two husbands. YVONNE GLADYS FLETCHER, whose first husband was initially found to have died of natural causes, was found guilty of poisoning her two young men with thallium. They were 25 and 30 when they died.
1954 : The world's first nuclear power station was
opened in the Soviet Union.
1960 : JOHNNY O'KEEFE was seriously injured in a car

accident. The Australian singer had face and neck injuries and skull fractures after his car collided with a gravel truck. O'KEEFE was returning to Sydney after a Queensland concert when the accident happened near Kempsey in New South Wales.
1972 : In Northern Ireland, the IRA began an
official cease-fire. It lasted for two weeks.
1976 : Terrorists hijacked an Air France Airbus with

250 passengers on board in Greece, and flew the aircraft to Uganda. The hijackers were demanding the release of 53 Palestinian prisoners. In a daring exercise Israeli commandos stormed the Entebbe airport and rescued the hostages, a week after the hijack. The seven hijackers, three hostages and one commando were killed in the rescue raid.
1986 : In the Hague, the World Court ruled that U.S.
President RONALD REAGAN breached international law by aiding Nicaraguan Contra rebels.
1987 : Former Liberal Party leader SIR BILLY SNEDDEN
was found dead in a bed in a Sydney motel. He was 60 years old, and had died of a heart attack. He led the Liberal Party from 1972 to 1975 when he was replaced by MALCOLM FRASER.
1989 : ALAN BOND vowed to fight to retain his media

interests after the Australian Broadcasting Tribunal ruled that he was not " a fit and proper person" to hold radio and television licences. The tribunal criticised Mr BOND's attempts "at deceit" over a $400,000 defamation payment to Queensland Premier SIR JOH BJELKE-PETERSEN. Three months later the Federal Court criticised the tribunal and set its finding against ALAN BOND. Two months later Bond Corporation auditors revealed the company had made a record loss of $980 million in the previous year.
1995 : Qatar's Crown Prince Sheikh HAMAD bin KHALIFA
al-THANI ousted his father in a bloodless palace coup but the deposed emir declared defiantly that he remained the legitimate ruler of the Gulf state.
